section: Nanotechnology - nature, scope, applications, Nano Mission, health and environmental concerns
subsections: Tools and synthesis - STM, AFM, top-down vs bottom-up

accepted.s: The Nano Mission was launched in which year as an umbrella programme under the Department of Science and Technology?
accepted.x: The Nano Mission was launched in 2007 under the Department of Science and Technology as an umbrella programme.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the launch year and implementing department.

accepted.s: The initial outlay of the Nano Mission was approximately:
accepted.x: The Nano Mission had an initial outlay of Rs 1,000 crore for a period of five years.
accepted.tq: Match the programme with its distinctive outlay and duration.

accepted.s: The Nano Mission continues as a national programme under which department?
o: Department of Scientific and Industrial Research
accepted.x: The Nano Mission continues as a national programme under the Department of Science and Technology.
accepted.tq: Use the ‘who handles this programme?’ authority test.

accepted.s: The DST Nano Programme had an allocation of Rs 350 crore in which financial year?
accepted.x: The DST Nano Programme had an allocation of Rs 350 crore in financial year 2024–25.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely placed financial years and programme figures.

accepted.s: Which one of the following institutions is associated with the continuing DST Nano Programme?
o: Indian Institute of Remote Sensing, Dehradun
accepted.x: The Institute of Nano Science and Technology (INST), Mohali, is among the institutions associated with the DST Nano Programme.
accepted.tq: Identify the institution linked with the programme rather than a nearby nanotechnology institution.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Quantum Mission:
1. It was launched on 19 April 2023.
2. It has an approved outlay of Rs 6,003.65 crore.
3. Its implementation period extends from 2023–24 to 2030–31.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The National Quantum Mission was launched on 19 April 2023, with an outlay of Rs 6,003.65 crore for 2023–24 to 2030–31.
accepted.tq: Verify the date, financial figure and implementation span as a single factual cluster.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Instrument)
 a. STM
 b. AFM
List-II (Characteristic)
 i. Can work on non-conducting materials
 ii. Images atoms on conducting surfaces

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: STM images atoms on conductors, whereas AFM can also work on non-conductors. Therefore, a–ii and b–i is the correct matching.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure instrument–function pair and eliminate codes that reverse the pair.
accepted.sec: Tools and synthesis - STM, AFM, top-down vs bottom-up

accepted.s: The Scanning Tunnelling Microscope (STM) is associated with which of the following combination?
o: Binnig and Rohrer; 1981; Nobel Prize in Physics in 1986
Binnig and AFM; 1986; Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1986
Rohrer and CVD; 1981; Nobel Prize in Physics in 1990
Binnig and Rohrer; 1986; Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1981
accepted.x: STM is associated with Binnig and Rohrer in 1981, and they received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1986 for related work.
accepted.tq: Match the instrument with its inventors, year and Nobel recognition.
accepted.sec: Tools and synthesis - STM, AFM, top-down vs bottom-up

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes STM from AFM?
o: AFM images only bulk materials, whereas STM builds nanoparticles by sol-gel synthesis.
STM images atoms on conductors, whereas AFM can work on non-conductors too.
STM works on non-conductors, whereas AFM requires conducting surfaces.
Both STM and AFM require the specimen to be conducting.
accepted.x: STM is used for imaging atoms on conducting surfaces, while AFM can work on non-conducting materials as well.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two similar microscopy tools by their sample requirement.
accepted.sec: Tools and synthesis - STM, AFM, top-down vs bottom-up

accepted.s: Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) was developed in which year?
accepted.x: The Atomic Force Microscope is associated with the year 1986.
accepted.tq: Separate the closely related years of STM and AFM.
accepted.sec: Tools and synthesis - STM, AFM, top-down vs bottom-up

accepted.s: Which one of the following processes represents a top-down approach in nanotechnology?
accepted.x: The top-down approach reduces bulk material to nanoscale dimensions through processes such as lithography, milling and etching.
accepted.tq: Identify whether the process cuts down bulk material or builds from molecular units.
accepted.sec: Tools and synthesis - STM, AFM, top-down vs bottom-up

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Milling is associated with the top-down approach.
2. Etching is associated with the top-down approach.
3. Self-assembly is associated with the bottom-up approach.
4. Sol-gel synthesis is associated with the bottom-up approach.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Milling and etching reduce bulk material, while self-assembly and sol-gel synthesis build structures from atoms or molecules. Hence all four statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Classify each process before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Tools and synthesis - STM, AFM, top-down vs bottom-up

accepted.s:
Arrange the following processes according to the approach with which they are associated:
A. Self-assembly
B. Etching
C. Chemical vapour deposition
D. Lithography

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Etching and lithography are top-down processes, whereas self-assembly and chemical vapour deposition are bottom-up processes. The sequence grouping the top-down processes first and bottom-up processes thereafter is B, D, A, C.
accepted.tq: Classify the items by approach and use the grouping pattern to select the sequence.
accepted.sec: Tools and synthesis - STM, AFM, top-down vs bottom-up

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a bottom-up method of nanomaterial synthesis?
accepted.x: Chemical vapour deposition builds nanostructures from atoms or molecules and is therefore a bottom-up method. Milling, etching and lithography are top-down methods.
accepted.tq: Use the build-versus-cut distinction to identify the bottom-up method.
accepted.sec: Tools and synthesis - STM, AFM, top-down vs bottom-up

accepted.s: The approval of a nano-carrier Vitamin D3 product by the DCGI in August 2026 illustrates which current application of nanotechnology?
o: Nano-enabled delivery of a health-related compound
Use of STM for imaging conducting surfaces
Replacement of all conventional fertilisers by nanoparticles
Manufacture of quantum computers through lithography
accepted.x: The DCGI nod to a nano-carrier Vitamin D3 product represents a health application in which nanotechnology is used to carry or deliver a compound.
accepted.tq: Connect a regulatory development with the application area it directly represents.

accepted.s: Which of the following concerns has been raised regarding the rapid rollout of nano-urea?
o: The lack of long-term studies before widespread deployment
The complete prohibition of nano-inputs under a nano-specific law
Its inability to be absorbed by plants under any condition
The absence of any possible agricultural use
accepted.x: A major criticism is that nano-urea has been rolled out rapidly without adequate long-term studies. The concern is about evidence and safety assessment, not the complete absence of agricultural use.
accepted.tq: Find the specific criticism rather than an extreme or absolute claim.

accepted.s: Nano-inputs in agriculture are reported to have the potential to improve:
accepted.x: Nano-inputs can raise absorption efficiency, which is one of the proposed agricultural benefits of nanotechnology.
accepted.tq: Select the direct functional benefit associated with nano-inputs.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is identified as a legal or regulatory concern in the context of nanotechnology?
o: Nano-products cannot be subjected to any safety assessment.
All nanomaterials are prohibited from research use.
Nanotechnology is governed exclusively by the National Quantum Mission.
accepted.x: The absence of a nano-specific law is identified as a regulatory concern. The other statements use unsupported absolute claims.
accepted.tq: Reject absolute distractors and identify the stated regulatory gap.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the significance attributed to nanotechnology in the areas of agriculture, health and development?
o: It increases dependence on imported fertilisers and replaces all diagnostic methods.
It is used only for studying atoms and cannot support medical treatment.
It can help reduce fertiliser subsidy and imports, support frugal diagnostics and enable targeted cancer drugs.
It is limited to producing conducting materials and has no health applications.
accepted.x: Nanotechnology is associated with reducing fertiliser subsidy and imports, enabling frugal diagnostics and supporting targeted cancer drugs. Its significance therefore extends across agriculture, health and development.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that integrates the stated benefits across multiple sectors without using an absolute limitation.
